issues.title: A file or server request failed
issues.ruleTitle: A file or server request failed
issues.why: The page asked for something (a script, style, image, font, or data from the server) and didn't get it. Missing scripts and styles break the page; missing data shows empty or wrong content.
issues.fix: Check the address listed. If the file moved or was renamed, update the link; if it's a server call, check the server function is deployed and working.
issues.change: Check the address listed. If the file moved or was renamed, update the link; if it's a server call, check the server function is deployed and working.

issues.key: header-hsts|No Strict-Transport-Security header (GitHub Pages can't send custom headers; see the fix for the workaround or a host that can)
issues.title: Browsers aren't told to always use the secure address
issues.ruleTitle: Browsers aren't told to always use the secure address
issues.why: Without HSTS, a visitor's very first request can be sent unencrypted and redirected by an attacker on public Wi-Fi.
issues.fix: Send the Strict-Transport-Security header (max-age of at least six months). Most hosts have a switch for this.
details: No Strict-Transport-Security header (GitHub Pages can't send custom headers; see the fix for the workaround or a host that can)
issues.fixNote: This site is hosted on GitHub Pages, which can't send security headers. It needs a host change (or Cloudflare in front), which is a decision for you.
issues.change: Make the host send this header on every page.
issues.snippet:
GitHub Pages can't send this header. Options:
1. Publish through Vercel or Netlify (both read headers from a file in the code), or
2. Put Cloudflare (free plan) in front of the domain and add the header there:
   Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

issues.key: header-csp|No CSP header or meta tag (GitHub Pages can't send custom headers; see the fix for the workaround or a host that can)
issues.title: No Content Security Policy
issues.why: A CSP is a whitelist of where scripts may come from. If any bug ever lets someone inject a script, the CSP stops it from running. It's the main safety net against account-stealing attacks.
issues.fix: Add a Content-Security-Policy header, or a <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy"> tag when the host can't set headers. Start in report-only mode and tighten it.
details: No CSP header or meta tag (GitHub Pages can't send custom headers; see the fix for the workaround or a host that can)
issues.fixNote: This site is hosted on GitHub Pages, which can't send security headers. It needs a host change (or Cloudflare in front), which is a decision for you.
issues.change: Add a Content Security Policy. Start with the report-only version below, check nothing breaks for a week, then switch the name to Content-Security-Policy.
issues.snippet:
GitHub Pages can't send this header. Options:
1. Publish through Vercel or Netlify (both read headers from a file in the code), or
2. Put Cloudflare (free plan) in front of the domain and add the header there:
   Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https:; img-src 'self' data: https:; font-src 'self' https: data:; connect-src 'self' https:; frame-ancestors 'none'

Without header support, a CSP can also go in each page's <head>:
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https:; img-src 'self' data: https:; font-src 'self' https: data:; connect-src 'self' https:">

issues.key: header-frame|No X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors (GitHub Pages can't send custom headers; see the fix for the workaround or a host that can)
issues.title: Other sites can embed this page invisibly
issues.ruleTitle: Other sites can embed this page invisibly
issues.why: An attacker can load the page inside an invisible frame on their own site and trick visitors into clicking buttons ("clickjacking").
issues.fix: Send X-Frame-Options: DENY or a CSP with frame-ancestors 'none'. (This one can't be set with a <meta> tag.)

issues.title: The page has no search description
issues.ruleTitle: The page has no search description
issues.why: The description is the grey text under the title in Google. Without one, Google picks random text from the page, which usually sells it badly.
issues.fix: Add <meta name="description" content="…"> with one or two sentences (about 70–160 characters).
issues.fixNote: Claude writes the description from the page's own text; check the wording in the pull request.

issues.title: The main content appears late (LCP)
issues.why: Largest Contentful Paint is when the biggest thing on screen (usually the hero image) appears. Google's target is under 2.5 seconds.
issues.fix: Compress and resize the hero image (WebP/AVIF, no wider than it's shown), and preload it.
issues.fixNote: The tool shrinks oversized images itself; Claude handles loading order (lazy-loading, deferring scripts).
issues.change: Make the images smaller (resize to the size they're shown at, WebP or AVIF, about 80% quality), load images below the first screen with loading="lazy", and let the main image load first with fetchpriority="high".

issues.title: The page jumps around while loading (CLS)
issues.ruleTitle: The page jumps around while loading (CLS)
issues.why: Content shifting as it loads makes visitors tap the wrong thing. Google's target is under 0.1.
issues.fix: Give images and embeds a width and height (or aspect-ratio), and reserve space for things that load in later, like prices.
issues.fixNote: The tool shrinks oversized images itself; Claude handles loading order (lazy-loading, deferring scripts).
issues.change: Give every image and embed a width and height (or CSS aspect-ratio) so the page doesn't jump while loading.

issues.title: A script from another company's server isn't locked to a version
issues.ruleTitle: A script from another company's server isn't locked to a version
issues.why: If that server is ever hacked or the library publishes a bad update, the changed code runs on your site with your visitors' sessions.
issues.fix: Pin the exact version in the address and add an integrity hash, or copy the file into your own site.
issues.change: Copy the library into the site (or pin its exact version and add an integrity hash) instead of loading a version that updates itself.

issues.key: header-referrer|No Referrer-Policy header or meta tag
issues.title: No referrer policy
issues.why: Full page addresses (which can include sign-in tokens or order details) may be passed to other sites the visitor goes to.
issues.fix: Send Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, or add <meta name="referrer" content="strict-origin-when-cross-origin">.

issues.title: The page doesn't name its main address
issues.ruleTitle: The page doesn't name its main address
issues.why: Pages reachable at several addresses (with and without .html, with tracking codes) can be counted as duplicates by search engines.
issues.fix: Add <link rel="canonical" href="https://…/page/"> with the page's preferred address.

issues.title: Links to this page share without a preview
issues.ruleTitle: Links to this page share without a preview
issues.why: When someone shares the page on WhatsApp, Facebook or LinkedIn, it appears as a bare link instead of a card with an image and title.
issues.fix: Add Open Graph tags: og:title, og:description, og:image (1200×630) and og:url.
issues.change: In the <head> of /, /manas-kaziranga/, /pyrenees/, /iceland/, /iberian-lynx/, add share-preview tags (the image should be 1200×630):

<meta property="og:description" content="…">
<meta property="og:image" content="https://tours.mw.photography/share.jpg">
<meta property="og:url" content="https://tours.mw.photography/">

issues.ruleTitle: The page title is too short or too long

issues.fix: Aim for 30–60 characters that say what the page is and who it's from.
